subject: Post-call: caching assumptions & pricing follow-up (FintechCo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@fintechco.com>, FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & follow-ups — caching assumptions for pricing

Thanks again for your time today, Sophie — great conversation. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can firm up the pricing sketch I promised: 

Call recap (high level)
- Primary flow: end user -> UI -> Redwood chat/generation endpoint (system + user + few-turn history).
- Expected load: a mix of personalization + templated prompts (we discussed a lot of repeated prefixes for certain workflows).
- Key buyer constraint: monthly budget target ~ $12k–$18k (you said this is the current planning range).

Asks / what we need to finalize a pricing estimate
1) Traffic estimates: monthly requests, avg input tokens, avg output tokens (or total estimated tokens/month). We discussed you could share a traffic CSV — thanks in advance.
2) Target unit economics: do you have a target effective $/1M tokens after optimizations (caching + model selection)? You mentioned wanting to get under ~$15/1M if possible.
3) Caching behavior: which parts of the prompt are re-used (system prompt, templates, user-specific prefixes)? Any known % of requests that hit on a cached prefix?

Quick note on how we model this on our side:
- We price on model tokens delivered; caching (prefix/KV) can materially reduce the number of tokens served to the model on many workflows, lowering your effective $/1M.
- Typical conservative hit rates for templated workflows: 15–30%. For more templated / bot-like flows we've seen 40–60%+ (depends on how many requests reuse the same prefix).

Next steps (proposal)
- Sophie: send the traffic-estimates.csv and any sample logs you can share.
- We'll run a short estimation exercise (Marcus + Aditya will model different caching hit-rate scenarios and show the impact on effective $/1M and monthly spend).
- If numbers look good, proposal & pilot (2-week technical pilot to validate hit rates).

Attachments: I attached our short caching playbook for context (redwood-caching-playbook.pdf).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & follow-ups — caching assumptions for pricing

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. Attached is a first-pass traffic export (traffic-estimates.csv) with our guesses for monthly requests and token averages. High-level numbers:
- Monthly active users: ~1.1–1.3M (we model to 1.2M for planning)
- Avg tokens per request (input + output combined): ~1,000 tokens (we're using longer responses for some features)
- Estimated raw tokens/month: ~1.2B (ballpark)
- Current planning budget for this feature: $12k–$18k/month (this is the finance-approved range for FY27 planning)

We don't have a precise hit-rate number yet — a lot depends on how many flows reuse the same templates and whether we push prefix caching into the client. For some templated user journeys we expect high reuse; for ad-hoc chat the reuse will be low.

Can you show a few scenarios with different caching hit rates and what that would mean for effective $/1M and monthly spend? Also please call out any assumptions on what we need to do on our side to realize the hit rates (e.g., deterministic prompt templates, keying scheme).

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Turner, Product Lead — Conversational Experiences
Sophie.Turner@fintechco.com | +1 646-555-2099

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & follow-ups — caching assumptions for pricing

Hi Sophie — thanks for the data, this is great. I ran a short set of scenarios below (keeping numbers simple so you can see the arithmetic). Assumptions first:
- Your monthly raw tokens = 1,200,000,000 (1.2B) per Sophie’s estimate.
- Baseline unit price (example model and instance mix we've discussed) = $22 per 1M tokens (this is the blended unit econ before caching/quantization; final quote may differ based on committed capacity / model variant).
- Caching hit rate = fraction of tokens saved across the whole workload (we'll refine with pilot logs).

Scenario math (easy-to-follow):
- No caching: effective tokens = 1,200M -> monthly cost = 1,200 * $22 = $26,400 -> effective $/1M = $22.00
- Conservative caching (20% hit rate): effective tokens = 1,200M * 0.80 = 960M -> cost = 960 * $22 = $21,120 -> effective $/1M = $21.12
- Mid caching (40% hit rate): effective tokens = 1,200M * 0.60 = 720M -> cost = 720 * $22 = $15,840 -> effective $/1M = $13.90
- Aggressive caching (60% hit rate): effective tokens = 1,200M * 0.40 = 480M -> cost = 480 * $22 = $10,560 -> effective $/1M = $8.80

Key takeaways:
- To hit your $12k–$18k target range, you need to be in the ~40% hit-rate neighborhood (or combine lower-cost model variants / quantization). For example, at 40% caching the monthly run-rate using the blended $22/1M figure is ~$15.8k.
- If you can (a) pin templated prefixes to deterministic keys, and (b) route highly-reused flows to a cache-friendly path, reaching 40%+ is realistic for many enterprise workflows we've seen.
- Other levers that lower the blended unit cost: model selection (smaller base models for lower-critical flows), int8/quantized inference options (can lower baseline unit cost substantially), and reserved/dedicated capacity discounts (we can provide committed discounts that materially change the blended $/1M).

Next technical ask from our side to strengthen the estimate:
- A 2-week sample of request logs (anonymized) with prompt templates and token counts. We can run a simulation and produce an expected hit-rate and an optimized keying scheme recommendation.

I've attached a short playbook and a one-page calc (see redwood-caching-playbook.pdf attached) — happy to jump on a quick session to walk through the math.

Best — Marcus
